note: H1 headline lines were pre-released on 29 Sep and the EUR 490m / 9.5-10.5% guide was reiterated two weeks ago, so the report carries little new; the only live line is the forecast section, where any change is a downside skew (item 1), partly offset by a possible itemised data-centre down payment (item 2) on a name that moves 3-9% on no news.

Q3 is new and the stock sits at a record above three of four targets after the bar was raised twice in the final fortnight (item 0), into a quarter the company calls its seasonally weakest after an end-loaded Q2 (item 2); the easy mdexx comp (item 1) and Kitron's defence read (item 5, sourced URL so filed, not dropped) only partly offset.

Thin tape, one commissioned analyst and a company-level organic ARR of +15% (17% Nordics) plus 6 MSEK signed-not-live ARR in the Q2 report (item 1) point to organic revenue growth moving toward the 15% target the stock trades on, with the first full Infosolutions quarter (item 0) and a 1.5 MSEK board purchase (item 3) the same way; the bar is unsourced so sizes are capped.

The CEO buying four days before the quarter closed, with Chair and NEDs alongside (item 2), makes a profit-guide cut unlikely and the weak start is already in a 14% fall, so the residual is a soft Q1 headline (items 0, 3) against a sector reading 'in line' (item 1); Q1 updates have moved under 1% here, so the number is small either way.

A small forecast raise to fold in the 14 Oct acquisitions is likely but has not been rewarded on past reports (item 0), while the hunter's unprinted per-ordinary-share arithmetic after the June preference issue (item 2) puts growth below the 15% target that cost 3.1% at Q1, on a thin tape already down 16% on rates (item 3).

The guide was re-stated on 28 Sep with Q3 nearly complete and BetMGM is already in the +4.7% of 13 Oct, so what is left is the CFO's post-quarter purchase (item 0) against last year's pattern of giving the BetMGM pop back on TU day (item 2); shorts covering and a thin reiteration keep it near zero.

A 39bp rise in the 10y NGB plus a Norges Bank hike over a quarter in which the appraisers already cut NOK 1.1bn with rates falling (item 0) makes another negative value change and higher LTV the likely headline, with Q2's -4.1% on the same line as precedent; the dividend sits inside policy (item 1) and the two new leases (item 2) are already in the tape.

EQT XI activation is the undisclosed line and its sign is open, with no first-close release through 14 Oct a mild negative (item 0); against that the bar was trimmed into the print (item 1), listed markets rose over Q3 (item 2) and the exit tape was active (item 3) on a stock down with a peer group priced for private-mark stress.

The Q4 Networks gross-margin range decides the move here (Q2 fell 12.6% on the guide despite a margin beat) and the company's own 'impact builds in the coming quarters' on component costs leans it soft (item 2); the three-quarter habit of landing above the guide midpoint (item 0), a possible Transsion catch-up (item 1) and the inventory unwind (item 4) argue for the quarter itself.

The pre-close call guided NFT, costs and loan losses so the quarter is mostly priced; the swing is the buyback slot Nordea has filled two years running, with thin buffer headroom and growth-first language putting the expected EUR 250m programme at risk (item 1), against likely positive Q4 NII commentary (item 2).

The Q3 report is the first update on NOK 296m of PEM backlog flagged at 'significant risk of delay or cancellation' with no project news since (item 0), the revenue line compares against a milestone-inflated NOK 303m with only NOK 377m of 2026 deliverable backlog (item 1) and cash falls on Iwatani plus capex (item 2); order intake is pre-released (item 3), results days fell on 7 of 9 prints, and the stock ran +9% in five sessions into it.

A record backlog (+34%) and 1.08 book-to-bill meet a soft Q3 2025 comp (item 0) on the book-to-bill line this stock has traded up on for two reports, with September Swedish PMI at 58.1 and rising new orders (item 1) pointing the same way and no run-up to say it is priced; the hunter's in-session 14:00 CEST timing puts the reaction in the 10-14 to 10-15 window.

The first Swedish property Q3 held its yield requirement through the rate shock (item 1), so SLP's unchanged 5.9% Newsec yield plus a swap gain likely puts NAV near SEK 36 against a 32.2 spot that is priced for valuation pressure, and the Q3 deals step earnings ability up 3-5% per share (item 0); both are computable so sizes are modest.

Income from property management is the line this stock trades on and the Sergelskrapan vacancy plus higher average debt make a flat-to-down print likely against a high 344 Mkr base (item 4, Q1 fell 4.15% on this line), while the mechanical derivative gain to NAV (item 0), held peer yields (item 1), the wind-park gain (item 2) and September buybacks (item 3) are positive but mostly computable.

Both co-CEOs sold about 40% of their holdings at 340p mid-way through the half being reported (item 2) and the H1 headline will likely break the double-digit growth line every recent update led with (item 6), against a history where 'in line' updates were sold 2-3%; the beatable 6% organic bar (item 0) and covering shorts (item 5) are the upside case, and the Mawer reduction (item 11) is a sourced holder fact, not a duplicate.
